label: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species (taxon ids / assessments)
governance: Maintained by the International Union for Conservation of Nature with assessments produced by Species Survival Commission specialist groups and Red List partners under a documented assessment process. Reuse is governed by the IUCN Red List Terms and Conditions of Use (non-commercial; no redistribution of the dataset). No DOI for the database; citation is by version. NOTE: on 2026-10-31 every IUCN URL (homepage, API root, terms page) answered HTTP 403 to non-browser clients, so none of these statements could be re-read from the live pages during this assessment; they are taken from the vendored record and general knowledge of the resource and are flagged as unverified.
versioning: Periodic numbered releases named by year and update (the vendored record gives 'issued: 2025' and 'ids only; assessment version not retrieved'). Taxon ids are stable across versions; assessment categories change between versions. The API (v4) requires a token.
known_issues: Anti-bot blocking: all 24 recorded taxon-id URLs plus the homepage returned HTTP 403 during re-check, so no identifier, count or checksum could be verified by script.
The vendored record stores ids only and did not retrieve the assessment version, so completeness is intrinsically limited.
Terms of use forbid redistribution; only ids and pointers can be vendored, not assessment data.
rationale: The Red List is a governed, versioned, globally recognised authority, which would normally score near 1.0 on authority; it is scored 0.9 because there is no persistent identifier for the database and because the governance and licensing pages could not be re-read during this assessment. Assessments synthesise primary field data and literature by expert groups (independence 0.85). Authenticity of the source is not in doubt, but because nothing could be traced live, record-level authenticity and integrity for the vendored ids must be scored as unverified.
